entry.dc:title: Comparison of clay mining in underground and open pit mines
entry.dc:creator: Knissel W.
entry.prism:publicationName: Erzmetall Journal for Exploration Mining and Metallurgy
entry.dc:description: In an empirical investigation the mining operations for clay and kaolin in the Federal Republic of Germany are compared. Starting with a differentiation between open pit and underground mines, the mining technology in German mines is presented. For the reason of the high productivity and efficiency of the open pit mining operations with hydraulic excavators and truck transportation, the use of underground methods is limited to high quality clays. Therefore possibilities for the improvement of underground mining are proposed. The production of clay in open pit mining operations is subject to environmental regulations. By an environmentally sound design of waste dumps and the use of a new drilling method for clay production, surface use can be minimized.

entry.dc:title: Effective modelling for cast blasting
entry.dc:creator: Chung S.H.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
entry.dc:description: There is a need for cast bla;. ing in open pit mining. Although this type of blasting requires higher explosive consumption, the 30 to 40% saving on handling broken muck justifies application of this technique. Based on the HEAVE module built in SABREX, a computer blast simulation program developed by ICI, effective cast blasting for different site conditions can be designed and confirmed by means of high speed photography. Case studies given in the paper confirm the model's ability to make realistic predictions. © 1989, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: Application of drive systems for mine haulage vehicles
entry.dc:creator: Johnson J.W.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
entry.dc:description: There are many different types of open pit mining operations around the world, and the challenge for any drive system manufacturer is to produce a system or systems that will work satisfactorily in these mines. Several factors must be considered, such as vehicle speed requirements, available engine horsepower, mine rolling resistance, grades, grade lengths, payload and tire sizes. How well a particular drive system performs depends on size, weight, and available tractive/retarding effort. In addition to performance, the system must also have an operating cost that will be acceptable over the life of the equipment. Today the choice of drive systems is between mechanical or electrical and within these types there are several manufacturers. Regardless of how the power is provided to the rear wheels, the job must be accomplished reliably and at acceptable cost. This paper will cover characteristics of an electric drive system and how it is applied. © 1989, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: Australian miners face up to deeper overburden
entry.dc:creator: Runge I.
entry.dc:description: Over the last two decades, the coal mining industry in Australia has developed into the world's largest exporter, and the mines have achieved recognition as some of the worlds most technologically advanced. Whilst Australian companies have not been slow to adopt new technologies in underground mining, the majority of growth since 1969 has been in the large scale open pit mining areas in Central Queensland and the Hunter Valley of NSW. With most operators reconciled to the changed marketing and financing positions of their coal projects, the challenge for the 1990's will be technical. Surplus capacity in overburden removal equipment no longer exists - and as the mines move into deeper areas, low cost dragline methods are increasingly less applicable. The article describes the equipment used at a number of Australian mines.

entry.dc:title: A mathematical programming approach for scheduling equipment in a surface coal mining operation
entry.dc:creator: Goodman G.V.R.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Mining and Geological Engineering
entry.dc:description: A mathematical programming model for scheduling open pit mining was developed and validated using data from a surface mining operation. A two-phase solution procedure was used involving repeated evaluations of an integer scheduling model and a simple transportation model. © 1988 Chapman & Hall Ltd.

entry.dc:title: Influence of blasting on open pit economics
entry.dc:creator: Singhal R.K.
entry.dc:description: A survey was recently carried out to study the blasting practices used in the western Canadian surface coal mines. The economics of open pit mining is heavily dependent on the cost of overburden handling. Steeper slopes lower the volume of overburden to be handled. There is, however, a limit to which the pit slopes in any given situation can be steepened - steepening beyond this point could jeopardise the pitwall stability rendering it unsafe and might result in curtailment of pit production.

entry.dc:title: USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE METHODS IN OPEN-PIT MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Brfueggemann H.
entry.dc:description: This article is based on a specific application of open-pit mining - the exploitation of raw material for cement production - but its validity is not restricted to this domain. In recent years Krupp Polysius has established a software package for the computation of numerical deposit models, based on borehole samples and topograpical data. Subsequently an additional module was required to evaluate these models and deduce a suitable mining strategy, taking into consideration different constraining factors related to the process technology. All work was performed within the framework of a real, normal-scale example, but all concepts, designs and finished software components are set up to deal with general open pit mining applications - they are not restricted to this specific application.

entry.dc:title: OPEN PIT MINING PRODUCTIVITY - AN UPDATE.
entry.dc:creator: Nilsson D.
entry.dc:description: In this article the development of productivity in US open pit mining is first briefly described. The study shows that for strip coal mining, there has been a small but steady increase in productivity during the last decade. In 1986, the average productivity was some 5 tons of coal per employee-hour. For US open pit metal mines, there was a decrease in productivity during the late 70's; but during the 80's the average productivity increased again, and in 1984 averaged some 40 tons per man-hour (ore and waste). The study also shows that the yearly production level in an open pit greatly affects productivity. For US strip coal mines, productivity is twice as high in mines producing more than 1 Mt/y of coal than in smaller mines.

entry.dc:title: Modified tree graph algorithm for ultimate pit limit analysis. M.Sc. thesis
entry.dc:creator: Huttagosol P.
entry.dc:description: The use of computer models to design the ultimate pit limits during feasibility study and long range mine planning is becoming a significant practice in open pit mining. One of the limitations of determining optimal ultimate pit limits using true optimizing techniques has been a great deal of computer resources required. The maximum closure of a graph model, which is a true optimizing technique developed by Lerchs and Grossman, is extended for solving an ultimate pit limit problem. The tree configuration of the graph theory can be reduced to only connections between positive vertices. The extended method is shown to require less computer memory and processing time while yielding an optimal solution. -Author

entry.dc:title: Comparison of tripper-spreader combinations
entry.dc:creator: Meyer T.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
entry.dc:description: In future, the volume of overburden to be dumped will further increase as mining operations have to go down to greater and greater depths in order to expose the mineral deposits to be extracted in open pit mining. For this reason, the selection of the correct spreading system is becoming increasingly important. Thus, an optimal tripper-spreader combination has to be selected with regard to the actual dumping procedure and the geometry of the dump cross section. In order to guarantee economical mining of mineral deposits, despite the increasing costs of overburden removal, the machine system selected must also be examined with regard to its costs, operational safety and availability. Because of the complexity of the subject matter and the limited size of this paper, this is a contribution only to give a brief overview of the machines more commonly combined as systems and to present their most significant features in terms of type, method of operation, mass and cost effectiveness. © 1988, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: Practical considerations for developing an automatically driven open pit mining machine: Compact bucketwheel excavator
entry.dc:creator: Kolleth H.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
entry.dc:description: The era of electronic revolution Is here bringing changes to mining technology. The surface mining industry Is keen to be part of this changing environment. Efforts are being directed towords developing automated mining equipment. This paper, using the compact bucket wheel excovator as an example examlnes the theoretical and practical parameters which must be considered in developing an automated machine. © 1988, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: SCIENTIFIC BASIS FOR DESIGNING A FUTURE COAL MINE.
entry.dc:creator: Burchakov A.
entry.dc:description: An analysis of the development of the coal industry in the USSR over the last 25 years shows that its lags behind West Germany in improving its performance. Increasing open pit mining and changeover to hydromechanization of underground mining are the two lines of advance pursued at present but they have certain disadvantages. It is proposed that the most expedient would be mechanohydraulic underground coal mining. The processes of coal extraction, its transport at the coal face and along the preparatory drifts would remain mechanical. However, its transport to the day surface would be hydraulic via pipelines. Applications of this method to a Kuzbas mine is considered. Problems of working with coal slurries are examined.

entry.dc:title: The dredging of lignite from beneath the Danube.
entry.dc:creator: Pavlovic V.
entry.dc:description: The use of dredging technology for the recovery of multiple lignite seams is an extension of current dredging practice. This paper identifies the essential elements of the operating technology for the dredging of the lignite from the Kovin deposit on the banks of the Danube. The equipment required for the trial dredging programme is specified. This trial will allow complete data on the practicality of lignite mining by dredge to be gathered, which will enable the full scale mine to be designed. The mine will be planned to supply two 300 MW power generating plants with 5.5 million tons of lignite per annum. It is expected that this method of mining will reduce the environmental impact of the mine, be highly productive as it is fully mechanized, convert 300 x 166 tons of lignite from resources to reserves and reduce the cost per ton of coal mined by 60%, as compared with conventional open pit mining.

entry.dc:title: FUTURE DEVELOPMENT WORK IN AUSTRALIA.
entry.dc:creator: Thomas L.
entry.dc:description: Australia is a fortunate country with respect to resources. Large areas of the metalliferous districts are still not explored in detail, and the known reserves are far more than are needed for domestic consumption. Similarly, coal is known to exist in many inland basins. A deep coal mine in Australia is only 300 to 400 m below the surface, and there are many coal seams still available for open pit mining. Australia has a technical ability to work deeper mines, for example, North Broken Hill Mine is working Pb/Zn/Ag ore at a depth of over 1500 m. Mount Isa will be deeper than 1800 m, and the new Olympic Dam Mine at Roxby Downs will extract gold, copper and uranium ore to at least 650 m. Coal-mine shaft sinking and drainage, as well as metalliferous mining techniques are surveyed.

entry.dc:title: Investigation of Labour Conditions and the State of the Osteo-articular System in Excavator Machine Operators Engaged in Opencast Mining.
entry.dc:creator: Grigoryan E.
entry.dc:description: The working conditions of excavator operators and occupation related illnesses of osteo-articular system are analyzed. The hygienic evaluation of conditions in open pit mining under general vibrations and adverse microclimate is discussed. The result of X-ray examinations of spine and arms and changes in osteo-articular system are described.

entry.dc:title: In-pit crushing and high angle conveying in Yugoslavian copper mine
entry.dc:creator: Santos J.A.D.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
entry.dc:description: Plans for large scale open pit mining of the low grade copper ore at Majdanpek Copper Mine began after a 1949 exploration revealed an extensive ore body. Mining operations and haulage systems have progressed in phases exploiting the most current technology. Phase I (1960–1980) haulage system was by trucks only. Phase II (1980 to present) began to exploit the favorable economics of waste haulage by conveyor from a fixed, pit perimeter crusher to the waste dump, with dumping by mobile spreader. Phase III (scheduled for 1988 operation) will expand exploitation of haulage by conveyor by Installation of in-pit portable crushers, shiftable conveyors and an elevating high angle conveyor (HAC®) to lift the ore out of the pit onto an overland conveyor system to the ore processing plant. Design of the HAC and its suitability for the severe requirements at Majdanpek (250 mm [10<sup>M</sup>] sized copper ore at 4,000 t/h [4,409 st/h] for 93.5 m [307 ft.] of lift at 35.5°) is the primary focus of this paper. The Phase III haulage system affords more in-pit flexibility and optimizes total excavation for the amount of ore to be recovered. Present plans for the future are for extending the Phase III ore haulage system deeper into the pit by introduction of a second HAC to discharge onto the first HAC. © 1987, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: Examples of open pit mining instability
entry.dc:creator: Brawner C.O.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
entry.dc:description: Geotechnical technology for surface mining has become increasingly sophisticated as lower grade ore deposits are being developed. With larger and deeper open pits, more detailed and accurate investigation has become necessary during the past decade. Many variables influence successful open pit operations. These include ore grade, metal price, development costs, construction costs, mine design, stability and operating costs. With the great increase in the size of open pits to depths over 600 - 800 meters, the determination of pit slope angle and control of wall stability has a major influence on project economics. This paper briefly discusses preliminary considerations for pit slopes from a geotechnical standpoint to optimize economics and safety, describes recent developments in stability engineering and to illustrate a wide range of stability problems, typical examples are briefly reviewed. © 1987, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: Procedure and example of grade control in open pit mining
entry.dc:creator: Guibal D.
entry.prism:publicationName: Pacific Rim Congress 87 Proc International Congress 1987 Gold Coast Queensland
entry.dc:description: Grade control plays an essential role in the good running of a mine. The factors at play are many, starting from a good analysis of the geology and a correct sampling procedure. Once this is achieved (and it is an essential prerequisite), the problem is to adequately define which is ore and what is waste. This paper tries to show, through a small example, how simple geostatistical techniques (variography, and moving average or kriging), can help in accurately defining these limits in a geologically homogeneous zone, thus allowing optimal use of the available information. -Author

entry.dc:title: The use of integrated geological, geophysical and remote sensing methods in the finding of economic minerals for open pit mining, southwestern Venezuela.
entry.dc:creator: Rodriguez S.E.
entry.prism:publicationName: Improvement of Mine Productivity and Overall Economy by Modern Technology 13th World Mining Congress Vol 1
entry.dc:description: SW Venezuela is formed by Precambrian rocks, mainly complex granites, pegmatites, and alkaline intrusives. As the result of the complicated geological, metallogenic and structural history, the area, especially the Cedeno District of Bolivar State, has constituted a very important target for exploration. Since 1972 the whole area has been under research by the Geological Survey and Regional Corporations. As a result of integrated aero geophysical programs an important carbonatite body was discovered in a jungle-type terrain. Geological, geo-chemical and drilling programs defined >400 mill. metric tons of a rare earth-Th-Cb-Ba-phosphate rich ore. Apparently, this carbonatite forms part of an extensive belt of intrusives of alkaline nature. Geological and geomorphological studies carried out in the extensive plateau of the Parguaza Granite, outlined more than 300 mill. metric tons of high quality bauxite during 1977. A large open pit is under preparation in order to produce raw material for the large alumina plant of Puerto Ordaz, Bolivar State. A large concentration of diamantiferous young alluvial sediments was outlined by remote sensing methods in the Guaniamo River Area. The ore bodies are constituted by old channels covered by a thick tropical rain forest. The deposits are under open pit mining. Between 1982 and 1985, Venezuela produced >1 400 000 carats of diamonds. Very detailed geological, lithological, geomorphological and remote sensing programs carried out between 1978 and 1982 in the Cedeno District, Bolivar State, defined several important Ta-Nb-Sn rich pegmatites. The intense wathering has produced a large and thick alluvial and elluvial deposits of gravel rich in Tantalite, Columbite and Cassiterite. Some specific areas are under drilling in order to outline ore bodies for open pit methods. Parallel to these investigations, the geological survey is evaluating important high quality quartz and potassic feldspar deposits.-Author

entry.dc:title: PRESENT STATUS FOR DEVELOPMENT OF TAR SAND OIL RESOURCES AND PROGRESS OF UPGRADING TECHNOLOGIES.
entry.dc:creator: Fujita M.
entry.dc:description: Tar sand oil is one of valuable hydrocarbon resources with approximate 1. 57 trillion bbl of reserve found in Canada. Two mining methods, viz. open pit mining and insitu recovery method, are currently commercialized and the latter will predominate in future. In Japan, Research Association for Petroleum Alternatives Development (RAPAD) was organized under the sponsorship of MITI and this association has been engaged in development of upgrading technology of tar sand oil for the past 8 years, with excellent results. Problems and countermeasures in production of tar sand oil and their import to Japan are also discussed.

entry.dc:title: A microcomputer approach for simulating truck haulage systems in open pit mining
entry.dc:creator: Castillo D.
entry.dc:description: A low cost microcomputer system for simulating truck haulage in open pit mining is presented. An actual analysis of a working mine evaluating computer dispatching is described. The system employs SLAM II and FITPLUS for simulating and statistically analyzing mining models. Issues concerning simulation software, statistical support software, processing times and implementation costs are addressed. Results demonstrate that with the proper tools simulation can be performed on microcomputers in an accurate, timely and cost-effective manner. © 1987.

entry.dc:title: Settlement observations of open pit mine backfill
entry.dc:creator: Thomson S.
entry.dc:description: Reclaimed land from open pit mining operations must have essentially completed settling under self-weight and must be capable of supporting light structures before it can be returned to the public domain. The settlement of the spoil from one open pit mining operation west of Edmonton, Alberta, was monitored by a series of magnet extensometers installed in boreholes. Time-settlement plots indicated that self-weight settlement occurs within a 3 to 5 year period. Tests of individual small footings pointed out the necessity to place shallow foundations on beneficiated soil. The results of a second series of small footings led to the founding of an 8 m×10 m prototype instrumented, reinforced foundation on a 1 m thick soil/flyash mat. Observations to date indicated an entirely acceptable settlement pattern.

entry.dc:title: Open Pit Mining of Petroleum Bituminous Rocks at the Kirmaku Deposit.
entry.dc:creator: Dzhavadov A.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestia Vyssih Ucebnyh Zavedenij Neft I Gaz
entry.dc:description: Petroleum bituminous rocks are a form of accumulation of hydrocarbons which are characterized by a complete or partial loss of mobility. The largest accumulations of such minerals are in the Sarmatian and Chokrakian tiers, in the Maikopian suite and in the productive formations of the Azerbaijan SSR. Some specific feature of open pit mining of these minerals are described. The plasticity of oil sands increases in summer and this creates some difficulties for excavation and transportation. The burden layer is only 2. 5 m thick.

entry.dc:title: LOS PELAMBRES COPPER PROJECT, CHILE.
entry.dc:creator: Atkinson W.
entry.prism:publicationName: Transactions of the American Institute of Mining Metallurgical and Petroleum Engineers Society
entry.dc:description: The porphyry copper deposit at Los Pelambres is a resource exceeding 2 Gt (2. 2 billion st) of 0. 7% copper and 0. 02% molybdenum. It includes a high-grade zone of plus 1% copper that is amenable to open pit mining with a low stripping ratio. Metallurgical testing has recoveries of 96% for copper and 93% for molybdenum which can be obtained by conventional flotation methods. This paper summarizes the history of the prospect, the geology of the ore body and the surrounding area, and the results of exploration.

entry.dc:title: BENTONITE GAINS GROUND IN US MINE.
entry.dc:creator: Gordon C.
entry.dc:description: Bentonite, rather than synthetic liners, is the preferred ground consolidation technique in Europe. In the US it is going through a trial period in the Montana Tunnels gold mine which is one of the bigger open pit mining projects in the USA.
